newsitem.title: UK: TENNIS-NOVOTNA FRUSTRATED AS RAIN WINS THE DAY.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-NOVOTNA FRUSTRATED AS RAIN WINS THE DAY.

text.p: Jana Novotna was serving for the match against Ai Sugiyama when rain stopped play for the day in the quarter-finals at the Eastbourne women's grasscourt tournament on Friday.

Novotna, the second seed, was one set up and leading 6-5 in the second when the umpire called for the covers to be put on Devonshire Park's centre court after 74 minutes of play. Steady rain continued all day.

It was the second successive day that rain had washed out all but a short period of play and organisers will now be hard-pushed to complete the tournament before the Wimbledon championships begin on Monday.
Natalia Zvereva of Belarus was leading Frenchwoman Nathalie Tauziat 6-4 5-7 2-1 in their quarter-final when the rain started.
Thursday was originally scheduled to be quarter-final day at this traditional Wimbledon warm-up event but showers meant that only 41 minutes of play were possible.

Defending champion Monica Seles was trailing Brenda Schultz-McCarthy 5-7 2-2 when play was abandoned on Thursday. Their quarter-final was rescheduled to Friday but organisers decided to put Novotna on centre court first because the Czech also had to fit in a doubles quarter-final, and possible semifinal, with American partner Mary Joe Fernandez.
Spaniard Arantxa Sanchez Vicario, the fourth seed, was due to play Romanian Irina Spirlea in the other singles quarter-final but, like Seles and Schultz-McCarthy, did not hit a single ball on Friday.

Sugiyama, who had trouble with cramp, was unable to cope with Novotna's skilful serve-and-volley game in the first set and obligingly provided a double fault to give the Czech the second break which put her 5-2 up.
Despite her obvious irritation at the chilly wind, Novotna won the final game to love, ending with an ace.
Sugiyama coped better in the second set, breaking Novotna to go 2-0 up. But she hit a double fault in the next game, helping Novotna to break straight back.
Another break in the 11th game put Novotna 6-5 up but rain was already falling and at 15-15 in the next game play was called off.

Organisers said play could continue on Sunday if the now-crowded programme of quarter-finals, semifinals and finals was not completed on Saturday, though the extension is unlikely to be popular with players
